BEHIND THE MODEL

Real principles.
A simplified machine.

This is an educational cutaway of a representative, vapor-fueled LPG forklift. Component locations are separated for visibility. It is not a manufacturer-specific design or an operating guide.

What the animation models

  • A four-stroke spark-ignition engine, shown as one representative cylinder, drives a fixed-displacement gear pump through a mechanical power take-off.
  • A 3-position valve feeds a single-acting lift cylinder. In neutral, the cylinder port is blocked and pump flow returns to the reservoir. Lowering meters oil from the cylinder to tank under gravity.
  • An ideal 2:1 moving-sheave chain arrangement doubles carriage travel and requires twice the load force at the cylinder. Real mast layouts vary.
  • The live example uses a 60 mm cylinder bore, a 10 cm³/rev pump, a 150 kg carriage and a 0.75 m cylinder stroke. Friction, leakage and acceleration are omitted. The illustrative relief setting is 120 bar.
  • Oil is almost incompressible. Moving dots indicate direction of flow, not air bubbles. Color indicates the circuit; oil does not change color under pressure. Mechanical cycles and lift movement are slowed independently for teaching.
  • The wheels stay still: the separate traction transmission, steering and mast tilt circuits are outside this lift-system view.
